evals.prompt: salut, faut faire évoluer notre feature de facturation. aujourd'hui on peut pas annuler une facture une fois envoyée, et on veut pouvoir le faire (avec un avoir généré automatiquement). y'a déjà des plans dans plans/facturation/ et le code tourne en prod. fais-moi le plan de modif stp, surtout pas de code hein
evals.expected_output: The existing plan files under plans/facturation/ are revised in place, never recreated. Reconnaissance reads plans/ and runs index_status/get_architecture first. Phase 1 produces a complete impact table in 00-overview.md (Module | Kind | Why | Evidence) before any plan is written, with a modified row for the invoice module and verify-only rows for ripple-set neighbors found via trace_path(direction="both"). The modified module keeps its existing NN-<module>.md and the plan-feat template, and gains the delta sections in order: Vigilance points and Anticipations first, then '## Current state' (verbatim search_graph/trace_path evidence — no claim from memory), '## Delta' (before → after table adding the cancelled status/transition and the credit-note behavior, every formula glossed in plain language), and '## Migration & compatibility' (live invoice data: migration, backfill, verification query, rollback or explicit user arbitration). Vigilance points include regression risk with a Gherkin scenario proving the old send behavior stays green. After each revision the strict coherence gate runs and is logged in the tracker; _progress.yml notes: records what changed, why, and when. Output is markdown plans only — no implementation code.
assertions: Impact table is present in plans/facturation/00-overview.md with columns Module, Kind, Why, Evidence, and contains at least one verify-only row backed by an exact graph call (trace_path) and its result.

The modified module's existing NN-<module>.md is revised in place — no duplicate/new plan file is created for an already-existing module — and contains a '## Current state' section where every claim carries the exact graph call (search_graph or trace_path) and its result.
A '## Delta' table lists before → after rows for the cancellation change (new status and transition), and every mathematical formula or state set in it carries a parenthesized plain-language gloss.

A '## Migration & compatibility' section covers live persisted invoice data with directive migration/backfill/verification steps, each reversible or with an explicit rollback step (or flagged irreversible with user arbitration required).
Vigilance points of the modified module include a mandatory regression entry with a Gherkin scenario on the old behavior kept green.

The feature tracker _progress.yml contains coherence_checks: entries with evidence (exact graph call + result, or quoted passage) after each revised plan, plus a notes: record of what changed, why, and the date; no implementation code appears anywhere in the output.

evals.prompt: Plan the addition of webhook notifications to our existing order-management system. Existing plans live under plans/order-management/ and the repository is indexed in codebase-memory. Requirements: (1) emit an HMAC-signed webhook on every order state transition (created → paid → shipped), (2) per-endpoint retry with exponential backoff, maximum 5 attempts, (3) subscribers manage their endpoints through a new CRUD API. Deliverable: updated and new plan files only — do not write any implementation code.
evals.expected_output: Calibration lands on Large (new modules and new relations), so the full pipeline runs. Reconnaissance classifies each touched element as existing / planned-only / absent with graph evidence. Phase 1 completes the impact table in plans/order-management/00-overview.md before any plan is written or revised: a modified row for the order state-transition module, new rows for the webhook dispatcher and subscription CRUD modules, and verify-only rows from the trace_path ripple set. Each new module gets a new numbered plan file using the full plan-feat template, after a search_graph existence check proving no existing module already owns that responsibility (never recreate an existing module). The existing order module plan is revised in place with Current state and Delta sections recording the added 'provides to webhook' relation. Phase 3 updates the relation map in 00-overview.md in place, marking each added relation with its justification, and derives the implementation order as a topological sort over modified + new modules (shared modules first). Plans are written sequentially in that order, each followed by the blocking strict coherence gate logged in coherence_checks:, and the run reaches done only after the final full-set gate on evidence produced after the last revision. Retry/backoff bounds and signature constraints are expressed as glossed mathematical notation and Gherkin scenarios. No code is written.
assertions: The impact table in plans/order-management/00-overview.md is complete before any module plan is written or revised, and it includes modified, new, and verify-only rows, each with an exact graph call and result in the Evidence column.

Each new module (webhook dispatcher, subscription CRUD API) gets its own new numbered plan file with the full plan-feat template, preceded by a search_graph existence check showing no existing module already covers that responsibility — no existing module is recreated.

The existing order module plan is revised in place and its '## Delta' table records the added relation to the webhook module; the relation map in 00-overview.md marks that relation as added with a justification and matches the plans' Relations tables in both directions (provides-to ⇔ depends-on).
The implementation order is a topological sort over modified + new modules with shared modules first, and plans are written sequentially in that order, never all at once.

coherence_checks: entries exist in the feature tracker with evidence for the gate after every written or revised plan, and the stage reaches done only after the final full-set gate runs on fresh evidence produced after the last plan revision.

Retry with exponential backoff (max 5 attempts) and HMAC-signature constraints appear in the new modules' plans as mathematical notation with parenthesized plain-language glosses and/or Gherkin scenarios; no implementation code is produced.

evals.prompt: Our password-reset feature has been in production for two years, but there is no plans/ folder and no design docs anywhere. We need to change it: reset tokens must expire after 15 minutes instead of 24 hours, and each token must become single-use. Produce the update plan.
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT redirect to plan-feat and does not refuse: the feature exists in code, so Reconnaissance step 4 applies — a minimal reverse brief is built from the graph (search_graph, get_architecture: modules, relations, statuses) before planning the change, with each touched element classified as existing (in code) and backed by graph evidence, never memory. The pipeline then proceeds: impact table in a new plans/<feature_slug>/00-overview.md with trace_path(direction="both") evidence, including verify-only rows for ripple-set neighbors (e.g. mailer, session/login handling) that are never dropped silently. The token module's plan carries '## Current state' (verbatim graph evidence of today's 24-hour expiry and reuse behavior), a '## Delta' table (expiry 24h → 15min, multi-use → single-use, each row glossed in plain language and matched to a revised Invariants/Behavior section), and '## Migration & compatibility' deciding explicitly what happens to live tokens already issued at deploy time (honored, revoked, or migrated) with reversible steps or explicit rollback. Regression vigilance is mandatory, every strict coherence gate is logged in the tracker coherence_checks: with evidence, and only markdown plan files are produced — no code.
assertions: The response does not redirect to plan-feat and does not refuse: it recognizes the feature exists in code with no plans and builds a minimal reverse brief from graph calls (search_graph, get_architecture) covering modules, relations, and statuses before planning the change.
Every element the change touches is classified as existing / planned-only / absent, and each 'existing' claim is backed by an exact graph call and result rather than asserted from memory.

An impact table exists in 00-overview.md with trace_path(direction="both") evidence and at least one verify-only row for a ripple-set neighbor (e.g. mailer or session module), with none of the ripple set dropped silently.

The modified token module plan contains a '## Current state' section with verbatim graph-call evidence of today's behavior and a '## Delta' table (24h → 15min expiry, multi-use → single-use), with every formula or state set glossed in plain language and every Delta row matched to a revised section.
'## Migration & compatibility' explicitly addresses persisted tokens already issued before the change (honored, revoked, or migrated), with each step reversible or carrying an explicit rollback step.
coherence_checks: entries with evidence exist in the tracker for each gate, the modified module's vigilance points include regression risk, and no implementation code is written.
